We are looking for a Senior Partner Deployed Engineer to join the Customer Solutions team, focused on building Coder’s partner ecosystem across EMEA. This is a new function at Coder, modeled on the Forward Deployed Engineer role pioneered by companies like Palantir and now the fastest-growing technical role at frontier AI companies. The difference: instead of embedding with a single customer to deploy a platform, you embed with strategic partners to help them understand, position, and deliver Coder’s platform across their entire customer base.

You are part Field CTO, part Industry Strategist, part Technical Specialist, and part Partner Relations Lead. You will be the technical authority within our EMEA partner ecosystem: setting the vision for how Coder fits into each partner’s AI, cloud, and modernization offerings, co-creating the GTM sales plays that partner sellers take to market, building the demonstrations and workshops that generate pipeline, and producing the Partner Relations content that establishes Coder’s technical brand in the ecosystem.

This is not a support role. You are equally comfortable holding a strategic roadmap conversation with a partner CTO and debugging a Kubernetes deployment in a partner’s lab in the same afternoon. You are energized by the challenge of building a new category through partnerships, motivated by the multiplied impact of enabling an entire ecosystem rather than a single customer, and capable of operating with full autonomy in a fast-moving startup environment.

What You’ll Do

  • Serve as the strategic technical thought partner to EMEA partner leadership, including practice leads, CTOs, and solutions architects at global systems integrators, regional cloud consultancies, and hyperscaler field teams. Own the technical relationship and set the vision for how Coder fits into each partner’s AI and modernization portfolio.

  • Co-create sales plays tailored to each partner’s customer base, vertical focus, and services capabilities. Author Working Backwards outcome proposals for strategic partner-customer combinations that translate AI Development Infrastructure into deal-level urgency.

  • Develop and deliver workshops, Builder Labs, and partner-hosted enablement sessions as the primary awareness and demand generation vehicle for the EMEA ecosystem. Build hands-on demonstration environments and interactive experiences that partners can use independently.

  • Intervene directly on the highest-value partner-attached deals across EMEA: co-sell calls, technical discovery, PoV scoping, architecture review, and technical win support. Own the engagement until the partner’s team can carry it independently.

  • Transform bespoke partner enablement sessions into structured LMS modules and certification tiers that scale across the EMEA partner base without requiring live PDE support for each new partner.

  • Produce “better together” reference architectures for strategic partner combinations across cloud providers and AI platforms. Include deployment diagrams, network topology, IAM patterns, and operational runbooks that partner SAs can hand directly to customers.

  • Codify each successful partner engagement into a repeatable GTM play: trigger conditions, discovery questions, positioning framework, demo script, PoV scope template, and expected outcomes. Build a playbook library that a new PDE or partner seller can pick up and run.

  • Build AI-powered self-service tools that automate high-volume PDE activities: Opportunity Brief Generator, PR/FAQ Generator, Workshop-in-a-Box deployment, and demo site builder.

  • Produce a monthly partner intelligence digest from EMEA engagements: what customers are asking for, how competitors are positioning, where integrations are missing, which vertical use cases are emerging. Distribute to Product, Engineering, and GTM leadership.

  • Own the EMEA-relevant portions of the joint technical integration roadmap with strategic partners. Define priorities cross-functionally with Product and Engineering based on field signals from the EMEA market.

  • Create and publish Partner Relations content, the ecosystem equivalent of Developer Relations: technical blog posts, cookbooks, partner ecosystem conference talks, enablement videos, and workshop recaps. Build Coder’s technical brand within the EMEA partner community.

What We’re Looking For

  • 7+ years of experience in a combination of Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Field CTO, Technical Consulting, or Developer Relations roles at an infrastructure, developer tools, or AI company

  • Demonstrated experience helping partners or customers understand and adopt products in emerging or undefined categories, not just executing playbooks for established ones

  • Proven hands-on experience designing and deploying cloud infrastructure on at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure), with production-level Kubernetes and Terraform depth. You have done the work and can speak to it with specificity.

  • 2+ years deploying or operating AI coding agents in a production or near-production environment: you understand how agent loops execute, where credentials live, and what governance and audit requirements look like in a European enterprise context

  • Ability to articulate the architectural difference between workspace-local agent tooling and a centralized agentic harness, and to explain why that distinction matters to a security, compliance, or data sovereignty stakeholder

  • Experience working with channel or technology partners in a co-sell model: hyperscaler partner programs, GSI/RSI partnerships, or VAR/distributor ecosystems in EMEA markets

  • Experience building repeatable technical GTM assets that scaled beyond your personal delivery: sales plays, enablement curricula, reference architectures, or technical content programs

  • Executive communication and Field CTO credibility: you can hold a technical vision conversation with a partner CTO and a deal-level architecture review with an SE in the same day, in English and ideally at least one additional European language

  • Strong written communication: you can produce a Working Backwards PR/FAQ, a technical architecture document, and a blog post without those being separate skills requiring separate people

  • Self-directed, analytically minded, and comfortable operating with full autonomy. You will define processes that don’t exist, build tools that haven’t been scoped, and create a function from first principles in a new region.

Bonus Points

(Bonus tacos? That’s how we say thanks at Coder. Ask us about it.)

  • Prior Forward Deployed Engineer experience at a platform company (Palantir, Scale AI, frontier AI lab, or equivalent embedded deployment model)

  • Track record of public technical advocacy: blog posts, conference talks, open-source contributions, or developer/partner community engagement

  • Experience with hyperscaler partner programs (e.g., ISV Accelerate, strategic collaboration agreements, co-sell programs) at an operational level

  • Familiarity with European regulatory environments: GDPR, DORA, NIS2, AI Act compliance requirements, and data sovereignty patterns for cloud-native deployments

  • Experience with air-gapped or network-isolated deployments common in European financial services, government, or defense contexts

  • Background in AI governance frameworks, session audit requirements, or SIEM integration for AI workloads

  • Experience with LLM gateway or proxy infrastructure (LiteLLM, OpenRouter, or equivalent) in a multi-team or enterprise context

  • Experience designing human-in-the-loop breakpoints or escalation patterns for autonomous agent workflows

  • Kubernetes certification (CKA, CKAD, or CKS)

  • Experience with Tailscale or similar overlay networking tools

  • Open-source contributions, particularly in CNCF, MCP, or AI agent ecosystems

  • Existing relationships with hyperscaler EMEA solutions architecture teams, European GSI technical practices, or AI infrastructure partner ecosystems

  • Fluency in German, French, or a Nordic language in addition to English

What Success Looks Like

  • You have done the hard technical work before: deploying cloud-native infrastructure, navigating Kubernetes in production, building with Terraform, and operating in the complexity of large European enterprise environments. You bring that credibility into every partner conversation.

  • You can walk a partner CTO through how Coder enables parallelized AI agents in a regulated European enterprise, covering credential isolation, audit lineage, GDPR-compliant data handling, and escalation design, and turn that conversation into a joint GTM play their sellers can run next quarter.

  • You translate deep technical knowledge into assets that scale: reference architectures partners hand to their customers, enablement modules partners consume on their own, and GTM playbooks partner sellers run without PDE involvement.

  • You are as invested in the pattern behind the engagement as you are in the engagement itself. Every bespoke partner interaction produces a reusable artifact. Every field insight feeds back to product. You codify by instinct.

  • You make the ecosystem and the product better: your field experience shapes how Coder builds integrations, how partners deliver, and how the EMEA market understands AI Development Infrastructure as a category.

Location: Remote EMEA (UK preferred)

About Coder

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. description:
Hi, we’re Bloom & Wild. We don’t just send flowers. We help our customers to care wildly. Caring wildly is celebrating the little things we all do for each other every day. Not just the big occasions. It’s being there for the highs. Stepping up for the lows.
 
We care wildly about people and our planet. Which is why we’re so proud to be a certified B Corp™ – committed to making long-term positive change for our community, and the world around us.
 
Founded in 2013, our mission back then was to make sending and receiving flowers the joy that it should be, by harnessing technology, brand and letterbox delivery. We announced £75 million Series D funding in 2021 and that same year acquired bloomon in The Netherlands and Bergamotte in France. Together, we’ve fulfilled and delivered over 20 million orders (and counting!), making us the largest direct to consumer flower business in Europe.
 
Now home to a family of 3 beautiful brands, we’re driven by our vision to create the destination for making life a little more thoughtful and beautiful. And we won't stop at flowers and plants. Starting with the Bloom & Wild brand, we're expanding our gifting offering to other categories like cakes, candles and cocktails. This is all part of our ambition to build Europe's #1 direct to consumer gifting destination. 

 

🛠️ The Commercial Team @ Bloom & Wild Group 

Our team cares wildly about delivering ambitious and profitable growth across all of our seven markets and three brands. We’re firmly focused on growing profitably, whilst also keeping an eye on the long term commercial view, and our wider business goals, in everything that we do.

This may sound like a cliché, but we really are a bunch of fast-thinking problem-solvers. Think Deeply, Act Swiftly really comes into play in our team. Our Slack channels are full of threads of our team coming together to solve a problem, sharing knowledge and resources, and all working together for our shared mission. We know where we’re headed, and we’re all ready to jump in to support each other to get there. We develop our commercial strategy whilst managing day to day trading to have full country or category oversight.

We’re a distributed team, and we currently have team members all across Europe & the UK! This role is based in our London or Amsterdam office with an expectation of being in the office 2 days a week (can be remote in Germany too), with full office presence and travelling to our Amsterdam office over peak timings. We work very frequently with almost all other functions across the business, so we’re really proud of our ability to collaborate effectively and are always looking for ways to connect and work together; making use of both our virtual tools and our lovely offices. We come together as a full team once a year in either London or Amsterdam for a team offsite, and throughout the rest of the year we gather in our respective country teams as frequently as we can! 

💻 What you’ll be doing: 

Reporting to our Commercial Director Germany & Austria, you'll own the trading function for Europe, one of our most important growth markets. You'll make sure we have the right stock every day, sell it to forecast and keep waste to a minimum. You'll also hold the pen on site pricing and make sure our website is set up to convert. You'll work across teams in a matrix structure, alongside our operations, central planning, range and product design teams, and play a key role in delivering our biggest peaks: Christmas, Valentine's Day and Mother's Day. It's a fast-paced, collaborative environment where no two days are the same and you can make an impact from day one.

Some of the responsibilities include:


Stock and forecasting:

  • Managing our day-to-day and week-to-week stock position with our central planning, flower buying and operations teams, keeping availability strong and balancing supply when there are shifts in demand and customer preferences

  • Making sure we have the volume and variety of stock available and sell it to forecast. You'll draw on past data, customer behaviour and the market calendar (e.g. public holidays) to keep waste to a minimum

  • Feeding into our longer-term forecasts, using customer insight and market context to decide where we grow specific SKUs and products. 


    • Pricing and range:

  • Holding the pen on site pricing, finding the right balance between selling price and margin, based on understanding of the overall product cost structure

  • Working closely with the range team on bestsellers, market needs and pricing architecture to ensure we’ve got a range of gifts priced for all customer’s shopping missions. 


    • On-site experience:

  • Owning the on-site experience, using stock levels, product naming and product ordering to grow or rebalance customer demand as needed

  • Making sure the right demand drivers are visible, and running the right tests for where the market is today

  • Managing the on-site AB testing roadmap from idea to launch for the European market and working with our BI team's insights to deliver next steps.


    • Peak trading:
  • Preparing for and delivering our peak gifting moments: Christmas, Valentine's Day and Mother's Day. You'll work with our forecasting and planning team to get order volume and delivery date forecasts as accurate as possible, maximising growth while minimising waste. 

    • Trading:

  • Preparing the regular trading meeting agendas and opening each meeting with the market context we need to make decisions across teams

  • Building strong relationships with our in-house operations, central planning, range and product design teams

  • Working with our UK and Netherlands trading teams and supporting trading in other markets. 


    • AI and automation:

  • Building and embedding AI tools and agents into our day-to-day trading, from automating daily forecasting inputs to spotting emerging trends in customer demand, so we can make faster, better-informed decisions. 

  • Collaborating on bigger impact  AI projects across our trading teams and other stakeholders in the business, so the best tools and workflows are rolled out across markets.

title: Senior AI Support Engineer (Paris)
description:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The role

Support at Dust is not a cost center. It is one of the most important product surfaces we own.

As a Senior AI Support Engineer, you will help define what world-class support looks like in an AI-native company. You will not just resolve tickets. You will own the systems, agents, workflows, and feedback loops that make support better, faster, and more scalable over time.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who has already operated close to support strategy, technical escalation, user experience, and automation. You should be excited by the idea of taking recurring customer pain and turning it into durable systems: better agents, better documentation, better internal tooling, sharper product feedback, and fewer repeat issues.

The best person for this role is not a traditional support leader who wants to manage a queue from a distance. It is someone with strong technical instincts, a deep user mindset, and a track record of building support systems that change how a team operates.

You might be a great fit if you have built an AI-powered support function, owned support tooling at scale, worked deeply with LLMs or automation, or carried a support strategy from problem discovery through implementation and measurement.

What you will own

Building the AI systems that make support scale

You will design, build, and continuously improve the AI-powered systems that help Dust support customers with speed and quality. This includes agents for ticket classification, auto-acknowledgement, response drafting, internal routing, proactive incident detection, knowledge retrieval, and escalation support.

You will identify categories of recurring issues and engineer them out of the support queue. Sometimes that means building a better Dust agent. Sometimes it means improving documentation, creating an internal tool, tightening a workflow, writing a script, or escalating product feedback upstream with enough context for engineering to act.

You will be expected to measure whether the systems you build actually improve the user experience. Seniority here means not just shipping tooling, but knowing what good looks like, instrumenting it, and iterating until the impact is visible.

Running complex support when the systems fall short

You will still be close to the work. You will investigate complex customer issues across logs, code, internal tooling, product behavior, and agent outputs. You will provide clear, accurate answers to customers, including when the underlying issue is ambiguous or technically complex.

You will handle escalated cases with precision and judgment, communicating clearly with both technical and non-technical users. You should be comfortable translating between customer language, product behavior, engineering detail, and business impact.

When AI-generated responses are incomplete, inconsistent, or wrong, you will debug the system behind them. You will improve prompts, knowledge sources, workflows, routing, tooling, and escalation paths so that the same failure mode does not repeat.

Shaping the support strategy

You will help define how Dust should run support as we scale. That means thinking beyond the queue and owning the full loop: what customers experience, what support sees, what agents can handle, what engineering needs to fix, and what product should learn.

You will translate repeated customer pain into high-quality product signal. You will build strong working relationships with engineers and product teams so escalations are high-context, actionable, and efficient.

You will also help raise the bar for how the support function operates: what we measure, how we prioritize, how we review quality, how we onboard junior team members, and how we decide what should be automated versus handled by a human.

What we are looking for

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

Wayve’s Robot Software group turns new vehicle programs into stable, reliable robot systems. The Platform Integration team works at the boundary between onboard software and vehicle hardware, bringing up new platforms while building reusable components and frameworks that make every future integration faster and more predictable.

As a Software Engineer on the Platform Integration team, you’ll combine hands-on vehicle and bench work with production software development. Your work will directly enable safe, scalable deployment across multiple vehicle programs.

  • Support software bring-up on benches, HiL systems, and vehicles, including work at international test locations.

  • Identify architectural improvements that reduce bespoke work and improve reuse.

  • Produce clear documentation and runbooks for long-term supportability.

  • Collaborate with hardware, safety, controls, calibration, and reliability teams.

  • New vehicle-program bring-up across embedded compute, sensors, networks, and software services.

  • Linux-based robotic and automotive systems with multi-process and distributed architectures.

  • ROS2 or similar middleware, node development, message interfaces, and system integration.

  • Sensor calibration, synchronisation, data validation, and system-level debugging.

  • Automotive-grade compute platforms such as NVIDIA DRIVE and Qualcomm Snapdragon Ride.

  • Vehicle communication systems including CAN and Automotive Ethernet.

  • Shared abstractions and frameworks that improve reliability across programs.

 

🙌 You should apply if

  • You have strong software-development experience in C++, Python, or Rust.

  • You have delivered production-quality software on Linux-based robotic, embedded, or automotive platforms.

  • You understand ROS2 or similar robotics middleware and distributed-system integration.

  • You have hands-on experience integrating software with vehicle or embedded hardware.

  • You can diagnose complex problems using logs, telemetry, on-target tests, and systematic experimentation.

  • You understand vehicle sensors, networking, and the practical realities of platform bring-up.

Experience with drive-by-wire systems, CAN tools, shared frameworks, HiL or simulation, functional safety, technical documentation, or observability would be valuable.

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial recruiter screen — 25 mins

  • Competency Interviews — Programming and technical domain (2 hours)

  • Deep-dive technical interviews — Programming, software design, and hiring-manager/team fit (3 hours)

  • Final interview — Mission and values alignment (30 mins)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.
